# Day Context (Calendar) — Architecture & Feature Guide > Single-source-of-truth labels (FOMC, CPI, early closes, weekends, holidays, > macro events) attached to every target row, daily stats doc, and report so > downstream consumers can stratify, caption, or filter days by what the > market was actually doing. ## TL;DR - A self-healing pipeline composes the trading calendar from three sources (CME holiday rules, FRED macro releases, hardcoded FOMC schedule) and publishes one canonical `dayContext` object per date to RTDB. - Every live target row (`ecTargets`) and every daily stats doc (`ecTargetStats`) gets the date's `dayContext` stamped onto it at write-time. Older docs are restamped automatically. - The Discord daily embed, the daily PDF (lean + enterprise), the weekly PDF "Noteworthy Days" section, and the dashboard's collapsible `Day Context` card all render off the same shape. - Two integration tests guard against under- and over-classification drift. - Annual maintenance is a 30-second paste-job in December (next year's FOMC meetings); everything else runs without human action. ## Why this exists Trading statistics without context are misleading. A 0/3 hit rate on a CPI day means something very different from a 0/3 day on a quiet Tuesday, and half-session holidays compress every time-to-target metric in a way that silently skews weekly averages. Day context lets us: 1. **Caption** every report so the reader knows what the market backdrop was. 2. **Stratify** stats by event type for analysis (e.g. accuracy on FOMC days vs. baseline). 3. **Filter** UI charts to exclude half-sessions when comparing apples to apples. 4. **Detect drift** — if the calendar were ever wrong, the integration tests fail before the data hits production. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph Sources["Calendar sources"] Rules["holidayRules
CME equity-index schedule
computeRuleEntriesForRange"] FRED["fredFetcher
CPI, NFP, PPI, GDP,
Retail, Jobless, JOLTS"] FOMC["fomcSchedule
Hardcoded 2021-2026
federalreserve.gov"] end subgraph Sync["Sync pipeline (calendar_sync.js)"] Compose["composeAll
rules + FRED + overrides"] Diff["computeDiff
past dates are immutable"] Apply["applyDiff → RTDB"] end subgraph RTDB["RTDB"] Special["calendar/specialDays/{date}"] Cache["calendar/_fredCache"] Meta["calendar/_meta"] end subgraph Stamping["Stamping"] Live["ecTargets (live)
stamps new target rows"] Daily["ecTargetStats daily
stamps daily doc"] Restamp["restampTrailingWindow
30d after every sync"] end subgraph Consumers["Consumers"] Discord["Discord embed"] DailyPDF["Daily PDF
lean + enterprise"] WeeklyPDF["Weekly PDF
Noteworthy Days"] Dashboard["Dashboard
SonaDailyContextCard"] end Rules --> Compose FRED --> Compose FOMC --> FRED Compose --> Diff Diff --> Apply Apply --> Special Apply --> Cache Apply --> Meta Special --> Live Special --> Daily Special --> Restamp Live --> Discord Daily --> DailyPDF Daily --> WeeklyPDF Daily --> Dashboard style Special fill:#4285f4,color:#fff style Compose fill:#ea4335,color:#fff style Restamp fill:#fbbc04 ``` ## Data shape Every date gets the same object at [`/calendar/specialDays/{YYYY-MM-DD}`](functions/features/calendar/calendar_postToFirebase.js) and a copy is snapshotted into each target row and daily stats doc: ```json { "dateISO": "2026-06-17", "classification": "regular", "eventTags": ["fomc_rate_decision"], "severity": "high", "session": { "open": "09:30", "close": "16:00" }, "note": "FOMC meeting", "sources": ["fred"], "schemaVersion": 2, "updatedAt": 1782102061818 } ``` Enums live in [calendar_constants.js](functions/features/calendar/calendar_constants.js): - **`classification`** (one per date): `regular`, `weekend`, `holiday_closed`, `holiday_early_close`, `late_open`, `macro_event`, `expiry` - **`eventTags`** (zero or more per date): `fomc_rate_decision`, `fomc_press_conference`, `fomc_minutes`, `cpi`, `ppi`, `nfp`, `retail_sales`, `gdp`, `jobless_claims`, `jolts`, `opex_monthly`, `opex_quarterly`, `triple_witching`, `futures_roll` - **`severity`**: `none` | `low` | `medium` | `high` | `critical` - **`session`**: `{open, close}` ET, or `null` for closed days - **`sources`**: which feeders contributed (`rule`, `fred`, `override`) A `regular` day with no tags and severity `none` is the default — readers treat this as "nothing special" and typically render no badge. ## Source modules ### `calendar_holidayRules.js` Pure functions returning the CME equity-index-futures schedule for any year: five full closures and five federal holidays demoted to 09:30-13:00 ET early closes. No I/O. Powers the `rule` source. > **Key design choice:** we deliberately use the CME schedule, **not** the > NYSE schedule. NQ futures trade on CME; some days (e.g. Columbus Day, > Veterans Day) are NYSE-closed but CME-trading. Using NYSE classifications > labelled those days as `holiday_closed` while live targets continued > generating, which the integration test > [`calendarConsistency.test.js`](functions/__tests__/integration/calendarConsistency.test.js) > now catches as a contradiction. ### `calendar_fredFetcher.js` HTTP client for the FRED `/release/dates` endpoint. Pulls 5 years of history on every weekly sync (see [Self-healing](#self-healing-design) below). Configured release IDs: | ID | Tag | Severity | |----|-----|----------| | 10 | `cpi` | medium | | 46 | `ppi` | low | | 50 | `nfp` | high | | 53 | `gdp` | medium | | 99 | `retail_sales` | low | | 180 | `jobless_claims` | low | | 192 | `jolts` | low | > **Why no FOMC from FRED:** the obvious choice would be `release_id=101` > ("FOMC Press Release"). It does not work: FRED returns it as a daily slot > for **every calendar day**, not just meeting days. We discovered this when > a deploy briefly tagged every weekday as FOMC. See > [`calendar_fomcSchedule.js`](functions/features/calendar/calendar_fomcSchedule.js) > below for the replacement. ### `calendar_fomcSchedule.js` Hardcoded list of every FOMC rate-decision day 2021-2026, sourced from [federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). Each entry is the second (decision) day; the module expands it into a two-day range so day-1 also carries the tag. This is the **only** input that requires human maintenance, and it's a one-line append per year. ### `calendar_compose.js` Pure function that merges rule entries, FRED entries, and (future) frontend overrides into the canonical per-date shape. Severity uses max-rank; `eventTags` are unioned; `note` is `;`-joined. Notable rule: on `holiday_closed` days, FRED contributions to `note` and `severity` are suppressed — a closed-market CPI release isn't a market event. ### `calendar_diff.js` Pure flat-map diff against current RTDB state, returning `{adds, changes, removes}`. The composite shape excludes `_meta` from the remove set. ### `calendar_sync.js` Orchestrator. Composes the calendar, diffs against RTDB, applies the diff, and triggers a 30-day trailing restamp. Three entry points export this: - **`calendarSyncScheduled`** — runs every Monday 06:00 ET (`onSchedule`). - **`calendarSyncManual`** — IAM-protected HTTPS trigger (`onRequest`); same orchestrator, for ad-hoc resyncs. - **`calendarBackfillManual`** — HTTPS trigger that runs `restampTrailingWindow` over a configurable window (default ~5y, max 540s timeout). One-shot deep history repair without needing a local SA file. ## Stamping pipeline The composed calendar is a source of truth, but downstream consumers (dashboard, reports, Discord) read the **snapshotted copy** that lives on each target row and stats doc. Two reasons: 1. **Immutable history.** A row written on a CPI day must remember that even if the FRED calendar later changes for any reason. 2. **One read, not N.** Reports don't have to join against the calendar at render time. ### Live stamping (write-time) - [`ecTargets`](functions/features/ecTargets/daily/ecTargets_postToFirebase.js) fetches `dayContext` for the row's ET date and writes it onto the row. - [`ecTargetStats` daily](functions/features/ecTargetStats/daily/) fetches it once and writes it onto the daily aggregate doc. - [`transformDailyToEnterprise`](functions/helpers/transformDailyToEnterprise.js) surfaces it at the top level of the enterprise payload so emails and the enterprise PDF can read it directly. ### Trailing restamp (catch-up + drift repair) - [`restampTrailingWindow`](functions/helpers/restampDayContext.js) walks the last N days (default 30), reads the current `dayContext` for each, and re-stamps every target row and daily doc. Shared between `scripts/backfillDayContext.js` (CLI) and the scheduled Cloud Function. - Wired into `calendarSyncScheduled` so any calendar correction propagates to recent stats automatically. ## Consumers | Surface | Module | What it renders | |---|---|---| | Discord daily embed | [`ecTargets_postToDiscord.js`](functions/features/ecTargets/daily/ecTargets_postToDiscord.js) | A "Day Context" field above accuracy | | Daily PDF (lean) | [`dailyReport.js`](functions/templates/reports/dailyReport.js) | Badge under the date header | | Daily PDF (enterprise) | [`dailyReport_enterprise.js`](functions/templates/reports/dailyReport_enterprise.js) | Badge + caution copy when severity ≥ medium | | Weekly PDF | [`weeklyReport.js`](functions/templates/reports/weeklyReport.js) | "Noteworthy Days" section listing every non-regular day with its tags | | Dashboard | `SonaDailyContextCard.js` in harper-vance-qa | Collapsible card; severity drives Bootstrap variant | ## Self-healing design Two systemic bugs taught us that the calendar must be impossible to silently drift, not just easy to fix manually. The current design: 1. **5-year fetch window.** Every sync pulls FRED with `realtime_start = today − 5y`. No matter how far back a downstream caller reaches, FRED will have served that range at least once per Monday. 2. **Past dates are immutable.** Both the FRED-cache diff and the composite diff filter `removes` to `date >= today`. If a release happens to drop off FRED's window or a rule changes shape, history stays intact. Meta records `pastRemovesSuppressed` for observability. 3. **Auto-restamp.** Each scheduled sync re-stamps the trailing 30 days, so any calendar correction propagates to recent stats/target rows without human intervention. `calendarBackfillManual` covers anything older. 4. **Loud regression tests.** Two integration suites under [`functions/__tests__/integration/`](functions/__tests__/integration/): - **`calendarConsistency.test.js`** — fails if any `holiday_closed` day has `targetsCreated > 0`, wrong early-close session times, or FRED tokens in the note. Catches *over-classification*. - **`fomcCoverage.test.js`** — fails if any of the 24 reference FOMC dates in the trailing 2 years is missing the tag or below `high` severity. Catches *under-classification*. 5. **Tested unit boundary.** 222 unit tests cover the diff algebra, compose merge rules, FOMC schedule expansion, holiday rules per year, and the sync orchestrator (with both fetcher and stamper mocked). ## Maintenance The whole feature requires one annual touch. **Every December** (or whenever the Federal Reserve publishes next year's calendar): 1. Open [federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). 2. Append the 8 rate-decision days to `FOMC_DECISION_DAYS` in [`calendar_fomcSchedule.js`](functions/features/calendar/calendar_fomcSchedule.js). 3. Append the same 8 dates to `FOMC_REFERENCE` in [`fomcCoverage.test.js`](functions/__tests__/integration/fomcCoverage.test.js). The integration test fails until both match. 4. Commit and deploy. The next Monday sync (or an immediate `calendarSyncManual` trigger) propagates the new dates everywhere. That's the entire ongoing maintenance burden. ## Operational playbooks ### Trigger a resync immediately ```sh TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token) curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ https://calendarsyncmanual-dbu3vf5feq-uc.a.run.app ``` Response shape: ```json { "ok": true, "counts": { "composite": {"added": 0, "changed": 0, "removed": 0}, "fred": {"added": 0, "changed": 0, "removed": 0} }, "restamp": { "days": 30, "targets": {"stamped": 142, "skipped": 0, "missingDays": 10}, "stats": {"stamped": 20, "skipped": 0, "missingDays": 10}, "failures": 0 } } ``` ### Repair historical drift (after a calendar bug fix) ```sh TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token) curl -sS --max-time 540 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ "https://calendarbackfillmanual-dbu3vf5feq-uc.a.run.app?daysBack=1825" ``` `daysBack` defaults to ~1825 (5y); override with the query param to scope the window.
